description: PLAYER REPORT (Battlewagon, tutorial T3 'Get Movin''): "the range circle is much further than I'm actually allowed to drag the model". Boots the real T3 lesson from the menu, disembarks the Boyz+Warboss, puts the Battlewagon into Advance through the mode radio + Confirm Movement Mode gate, then grabs the hull and drags 23" east - far past the 10"+D6 Advance cap - and HOLDS it so the clamped frame can be measured. 11e core rules: a model's move is measured 'from the same point on its base at the start and end of that move', and 'rotating a model does not count towards the distance it has moved'. So the budget is a plain centre-to-centre translation and the drag clamp (which stops the model's CENTRE at the remaining budget) is correct. The ring was not: it was drawn at remaining + Measurement.base_extent_px(model), the base's circumscribed radius - for this 100x180mm rectangular base 162px (4.05") of extra ring, i.e. the worst case over every facing the free 11e pivot allows. Asserts the base extent really is that large, that the ring is now drawn at exactly the remaining move, and that the held ghost lands ON the ring (ring - ghost == the terrain the stop point is charged, 0 on open ground).

steps.comment: OK on the native ConfirmationDialog - its internal button has no scene path for click_node
19.03: the attached Warboss disembarks WITH the Boyz. Before the fix the placement only asked for the 10 Boyz, reported complete, and left the Warboss aboard.
The Warboss model is actually ON THE BOARD at a placed position, not merely flagged as disembarked
Battlewagon is empty — neither the Boyz nor the Warboss are left inside
11e 18.04 - a tactical disembark from a transport that has NOT moved leaves the unit selected to make its own move; the new step teaches that affordance

PLAYER REPORT (Get Movin' step 4): beginning the disembarked Boyz' move used to paint one cyan 2" coherency ring PER model - 10 overlapping ~5.3"-wide circles on a tightly-packed mob, which players read as an unexplained engagement-range bubble. The rings are gone; the container stays (empty) so this assertion is meaningful rather than vacuous.

The OTHER two movement guides must survive the removal: the red enemy engagement-range rings (MovementERVisual) are still populated on move-begin, and the per-model green reach circle container (MoveRangeVisual, filled on pickup) still exists. Only the coherency rings are zeroed.

Carry m1 (board 480,500) 120px (3") straight up and HOLD it there - far enough that its nearest mate m2 at (544,500) is 136px away centre-to-centre, i.e. out of coherency once both 32mm bases are taken off. Paused with release:false so the carried-model ring can be inspected in both states, then walked back to the pickup point and dropped with zero distance so the Ctrl+A group drag below is the move that actually counts.
Proves the ring is live, not a static decoration: it recolours as the carry crosses out of coherency, from the same verdict that drives the label and the ghost lines.

Walk the carry back to the pickup point WITHOUT releasing - MovementController._unhandled_input routes any motion to _update_model_drag while dragging_model holds, so a buttonless hover moves the live carry. The ring must follow and flip back to cyan.
10-model mob -> 9 lines from the carried Boy to his mates, at least one of them green. This is the affordance that replaces the rings, so it is asserted in the same breath as their absence.

Follow-up to the ring removal: coherency came back as ONE ring on the model actually being carried, instead of T-094's one-per-model. This pins the count at 1, the anchor to the ghost, and the radius to base + coherency distance so an edition change to the 2" distance moves the ring with it.
The ring recolours from the same verdict as the label (cyan = coherent, amber = broken). Amber deliberately, not red - red is the enemy engagement-range rings.
Drop m1 back where it started - a zero-distance stage, so the 1" group drag below is still the whole of this unit's move and the downstream distance assertions are untouched.
and still no rings after the drop - the drag path must not re-introduce them either

the step must REMIND the player they can grab the whole mob at once - 11 models dragged one at a time is the slow path players fall into right after a disembark. {key:select_all} renders through KeybindingManager, so this also proves the token resolved (an unresolved token would read '{key:select_all}').
the shortcut the card now advertises

the card's claim driven for real: Ctrl+A grabbed every alive Boy AND the attached Warboss (MovementController._select_all_unit_models walks the bodyguard plus attached characters), which is the 'all 11' the prompt promises
selecting the mob is not moving it - the step must not advance on a selection

m1 is at board (480,500) after placement - dragging a SELECTED model shifts the WHOLE formation 40px (1") (MovementController._start_group_movement), well inside the 6" cap and coherency. Away from the wagon, not towards it: the Battlewagon hull spans board x 561-719 / y 178-462, so a 1" step towards it puts the middle of the front rank inside the hull and only the two outer Boyz can be placed. PAUSED here (release:false) purely so the group carry can be inspected mid-flight for coherency rings; mouse_up_board below completes the identical drop.

The original regression, pinned at its worst case: a GROUP carry of all 11 models must paint NO coherency rings. A group carry translates every selected model rigidly so the distances between them cannot change, and one ring per carried model is exactly the wall of cyan a player reported after disembarking the mob.
staging a model must NOT advance the step - it waits for the move to be locked in
the Boy really moved - guards against a zero-distance stage passing for a move (staged moves only reach GameState on CONFIRM_UNIT_MOVE, so this reads the live move data)

Let the group-drop staging pipeline drain before counting. MovementController._end_group_drag emits one STAGE_MODEL_MOVE per model with a 0.01s gap, then waits 0.1s and re-sends any straggler - for an 11-model mob that is ~2s of real time once each action's phase processing is included. The group_drop_in_flight assertion below is the actual gate; this wait just gets us there.

The staging batch has finished. Without this gate the all-11 assertion below can read model_distances mid-batch and report the last models as 'did not move' when they stage a frame later - a false failure that says nothing about the feature.

'one drag shifts da whole mob' proven end to end: ONE drag off ONE selected model staged real distance for EVERY alive Boy and the attached Warboss. This is also the regression pin for the group-drag key collision - group_drag_start_positions used to be keyed by bare model_id, so the Warboss ('m1') inherited the first Boy's start position, was sent to the BOY's destination, and the phase rejected it as 'Distance 7.5" exceeds cap 6.0"'. He never moved, and the two Boyz whose destinations he was still standing in were blocked behind him - 8 of 11 placed instead of 11.

steps.script:
var o = tree.root.get_node("/root/TutorialOverlay")
return o.current_body_text().contains("End This Unit's Move")
steps.comment: REPORTED: the step never told the player the move has to be locked in - they dropped the mob and waited. The card must NAME the button (the done-gate has always been CONFIRM_UNIT_MOVE, so a body that stops at 'drops da lot' is a dead end).
the standing reminder: box one ticks off the drag, box two stays OPEN so the outstanding confirm is visible on the card rather than only in a sentence the player already scrolled past
and it is actually RENDERED - current_checklist_text() is empty when the row is hidden

anchor_when: with the models down, the spotlight has walked off the mob (anchor {unit: U_BOYZ_T}) and onto the button the card is now telling the player to press. Before the fix the ring stayed on the Boyz - pointing at the thing they had already done.
confirming the move wrote the new position through to GameState

REPORTED BUG ('it says tutorial_locked when I select Advance'): MovementController._on_confirm_mode_pressed emits BEGIN_ADVANCE and then LOCK_MOVEMENT_MODE from ONE click, and BEGIN_ADVANCE completes wagon_mode synchronously (phase_action_taken -> _check_done -> _advance_step). So the second half of that click is gated by keep_da_roll's allow-list, which was empty - the mode never locked and the player got a red 'tutorial_locked'. mode_locked is the observable proof the lock landed.
and the gate itself allows it - so a re-confirm cannot resurrect the toast

the dice popups must be entirely the player's — an injected 'Exit Tutorial' lands in the AcceptDialog's own button bar, which is a separate focus root from its content, and on a pad that took Keep Roll / Re-roll away from the D-pad entirely. Same dialog class the charge roll uses.
Keep Roll lives inside an embedded Window (AcceptDialog) - real-coordinate clicks into embedded windows are unreliable, the schema's emit_pressed escape hatch exists for this

steps.script:
# The wagon is on a 100x180mm RECTANGULAR base. Measurement.base_extent_px is
# its circumscribed radius (half the diagonal) ~ 162px ~ 4.05" - the whole size
# of the discrepancy the player reported.
var mc = tree.root.get_node("Main").movement_controller
return Measurement.base_extent_px(GameState.get_unit("U_BATTLEWAGON_T").models[0])

# Frame the wagon and its whole reach ring for the screenshot.
var m = tree.root.get_node("Main")
m.view_zoom = 0.85
m.view_offset = Vector2(460.0, 400.0) - Vector2(960.0, 540.0) / 0.85
m.update_view_transform()
return true

steps.comment: Grab the hull and drag 13.5" WEST - past the 11" Advance cap (M10 + a rolled 1") - so the over-range drag clamp (SettingsService.drag_clamp_to_max_range, on by default) parks the ghost exactly at the model's remaining budget. West rather than east because the eastward corridor runs the wagon into a ruin, and terrain the clamp charges would stop it short of the ring for a reason that has nothing to do with this fix. Held (release:false) so the live frame can be measured.

steps.script:
# The stop point is charged no terrain, so the clamp's only constraint here is
# the move budget itself.
var mc = tree.root.get_node("Main").movement_controller
return mc._get_terrain_penalty_for_move(mc.drag_start_pos, mc.current_path[1])
